elaborations.text: Identify how texts construct perspectives, representations, attitudes, values, beliefs and cultural assumptions for particular audiences and purposes.

supplementary_resources.title: Representation Check
supplementary_resources.content: Name the perspective being constructed, the audience value it appeals to, and the textual evidence that builds it.

concept_card.core_rule: A strong senior response explains what representation is constructed, how textual choices construct it, and why that matters for the intended audience.

learning_objectives: Identify perspectives and representations in senior English tasks
Connect evidence to attitudes, values and beliefs
Explain how an audience is positioned

explanation_sections.heading: Representation
explanation_sections.body: Move beyond listing a topic. Ask what version of a person, group, place or issue the text constructs, then link that representation to language, structure or selection of details.

common_mistakes: Describing the issue without naming a constructed representation
Mentioning values without tying them to textual evidence
success_criteria: I can name a constructed representation and support it with specific evidence.
I can explain how audience values shape meaning.

elaborations.text: Use genre conventions, language features and structures to create public audience texts with clear purpose, context and audience positioning.

supplementary_resources.title: Public Voice Scaffold
supplementary_resources.content: Draft an opening that establishes context, audience, contention and a public-facing voice in under 120 words.

concept_card.core_rule: A public audience response needs a recognisable genre voice, a purposeful structure, and persuasive choices shaped for a specific audience rather than a generic essay tone.

learning_objectives: Select conventions that suit a public audience task
Create a persuasive structure for a feature article or speech
Control tone for context and audience

explanation_sections.heading: Public Purpose
explanation_sections.body: Public audience texts persuade by combining contention, voice, evidence and audience values. The genre should shape the whole response, not only the introduction.

common_mistakes: Writing a school essay when the task asks for a public article or speech
Using rhetorical questions without developing evidence or reasoning
success_criteria: I can make the audience and publication context clear.
I can use genre conventions to support a persuasive purpose.

elaborations.text: Control language features, grammar, punctuation, spelling, cohesion and referencing choices to support meaning and audience impact.

supplementary_resources.title: Senior Edit Pass
supplementary_resources.content: Run three passes: cohesion between paragraphs, precision of analytical or persuasive verbs, then sentence-level spelling and punctuation.

concept_card.core_rule: Textual features are assessed through how precisely language, cohesion and mechanics support meaning; editing should target meaning first and surface accuracy second.

learning_objectives: Improve cohesion within and between paragraphs
Select precise vocabulary for analytical, persuasive or imaginative tasks
Edit grammar, punctuation and spelling without flattening voice

explanation_sections.heading: Editing Sequence
explanation_sections.body: Edit paragraphs before sentences. Check whether the logic is clear, then sharpen verbs and evidence, then proofread punctuation, spelling and sentence boundaries.

common_mistakes: Proofreading only spelling while leaving unclear logic in place
Using vague verbs such as shows or talks about in analytical writing
success_criteria: I can edit cohesion and expression before final proofreading.
I can choose precise verbs and sentence structures for my task type.

topics.name: Analytical Thesis and Evidence

elaborations.text: Develop analytical interpretations by selecting, synthesising and evaluating evidence from literary or non-literary texts.

supplementary_resources.title: Thesis to Evidence
supplementary_resources.content: Write one thesis sentence, then list three evidence points that each prove a different part of the interpretation.

skills: Evaluate effects of aesthetic and stylistic features

concept_card.core_rule: Senior analytical writing should make a defensible interpretation, integrate evidence economically, and evaluate how textual choices shape meaning.

learning_objectives: Write a thesis that answers the analytical task
Evaluate effects rather than only identify techniques

explanation_sections.heading: Thesis Control
explanation_sections.body: A thesis is not a topic label. It should make a clear judgement about how meaning is constructed and should guide every body paragraph.

common_mistakes: Starting paragraphs with plot summary instead of argument
Dropping quotations without explaining their effect
success_criteria: I can state an interpretation that answers the question.
I can use evidence to evaluate how meaning is made.

topics.name: Imaginative Springboard and Aesthetic Features

elaborations.text: Create imaginative texts by manipulating aesthetic features, stylistic devices, perspectives and genre conventions for a stated purpose.

supplementary_resources.title: Springboard Plan
supplementary_resources.content: Choose one source feature to transform, one perspective to foreground, and three aesthetic choices that will shape the reader response.

skills: Explain aesthetic choices in a writer's statement

concept_card.core_rule: A senior imaginative response should use a clear springboard from a source or concept, manipulate aesthetic features deliberately, and sustain a purposeful voice.

learning_objectives: Plan an imaginative response from a source springboard
Manipulate aesthetic features for reader impact
Connect creative choices to purpose in a writer's statement

explanation_sections.heading: Springboard
explanation_sections.body: Use the source as a launch point rather than a copy. Transform perspective, setting, voice or symbol while keeping the creative purpose clear.

common_mistakes: Using decorative imagery that does not support purpose
success_criteria: I can identify the source feature I am transforming.
I can explain how my aesthetic choices shape reader response.
